title: Stochastic confidence-driven kernel fallback and on-demand recalibration for mixed-precision inference
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective:
Implement a runtime decision layer that selects between FP16 / FP8 / INT8 kernel paths on a per-request and per-layer basis using stochastic confidence estimates and a compact quality budget. The decision layer must prefer the cheapest kernel that meets an accuracy envelope, fall back deterministically when the confidence budget is exhausted, and trigger lightweight on-demand recalibration for edge cases observed in production traffic.

Why this work:
- Existing heuristics pick kernels solely by static calibration scores, which leaves tail-request accuracy and out-of-distribution prompts unaccounted for.
- We need a low-latency, low-overhead runtime mechanism to trade accuracy vs cost dynamically while preserving end-to-end latency SLOs.

High-level approach:
1) Per-layer micro-profiles: store compact metrics for each layer and model variant (mean error, variance, staleness timestamp). These profiles are produced by offline calibration runs and continuously updated from sampled production traces.
2) Confidence estimator: a lightweight per-request scoring function that aggregates prefix-token logits divergence and cached-KV similarity into a single confidence score between 0 and 1.
3) Quality budget: assign each request a tiny quality budget derived from route/model SLA, customer tier, and latency headroom. The estimator decrements budget per layer if kernel selection uses a lower-precision path.
4) Fallback policy: if budget would be exceeded for a given layer, route that layer to the next-higher precision kernel. We implement both greedy and probabilistic fallback variants for A/B testing.
5) On-demand recalibration: when multiple requests from a model/route hit repeated budget exhaustion with similar input features, spawn a background lightweight recalibration job (uses a small representative prompt set) that updates the micro-profile and potentially enables cheaper kernels without user-visible regressions.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Must not add >0.5ms median per-request overhead on top of serving runtime.
- We will not change model weights or full offline quantization pipelines in this ticket; this is a runtime dispatch layer only.

Telemetry and metrics we will capture:
- per-request selected precision per-layer
- confidence score distribution (p0/p50/p95)
- budget consumption histogram
- fallback events rate and latency delta for fallbacks
- post-selection accuracy proxy (sampled golden inference comparisons every N requests)

Rollout plan:
- internal canary on dedicated infra (10% of Dedicated customers) measuring latency and sampled accuracy regressions
- expand with weighted rollout to Hosted API workloads (route-sampled) if regressions <0.05% and median latency delta <0.3ms
- enable automatic background recalibration only after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and manual review

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: confidence estimator miscalibrated leading to over-usage of high-precision kernels -> mitigation: conservative default budget and offline simulation with production trace replay.
- Risk: recalibration jobs can be noisy or expensive -> mitigation: cap concurrent recalibrations per model and enforce evaluation gates before profile updates.

Deliverables:
- runtime decision module (C++/Rust) with a plugin hook for precision selection
- light-weight confidence estimator library used by runtime and SDK test harness
- background recalibration worker and bounded queue
- dashboards for budget/fallback/accuracy signals and alerting rules

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end prototype deployed to staging that shows <0.5ms overhead and can reduce average token cost by >=8% on mixed-precision workloads without >0.1% sampled accuracy regressions.
- Telemetry events emitted as documented + dashboard widgets built.
- Feature flags for greedy/probabilistic fallback variants and for enabling/disabling recalibration.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in staging with feature flag: 'confidence_fallback'
Median per-request CPU/GPU overhead < 0.5ms measured on staging traces
Average token cost reduction >= 8% on representative mixed-precision benchmark
Sampled golden-comparison accuracy regressions <= 0.1% after rollout to 10% traffic
Dashboards for confidence score, budget consumption, fallback rate, and recalibration events present

implementation_notes: Keep micro-profile schema compact: (mean_error_x1000, variance_x1000, last_calibrated_unix) as 3 small ints
Confidence estimator must be vectorized to run efficiently on CPU and avoid GPU roundtrips
Use existing kernel info registry (kernel_id -> cost_estimate, precision_tag) to compute budget consumption
